title: Still Waiting For EV Consolidation
text:
Still Waiting For EV Consolidation

Ernan Cui

Gavekal Dragonomics | 11 Sep 2026

China’s booming electric-vehicle market is now undergoing its first major correction: domestic sales dropped 13% YoY in the year to July, and there is little prospect of a rebound soon (see The Downtrend In Auto Demand). This downturn was widely expected to spur a shakeout among the dozens of Chinese EV makers, and indeed some smaller firms have exited the market. But among the top 16 EV makers that account for nearly all sales, consolidation is going into reverse as the two leaders, BYD and Tesla, cede ground to a combination of EV upstarts and legacy automakers.No members of this leading group are likely to exit the market anytime soon, so significant industry consolidation is not on the near horizon. Booming exports are helping many automakers ride out the domestic correction, and financial support from their state and private-sector backers appears secure—not least because there is a demonstrated path to take on the industry leaders by using specialist EV technology providers. At this point, only a decline in global demand for Chinese EVs seems a sufficient shock to force the industry into a major consolidation.
